name: hidden surprise lemony prawn pizza rsc
ingredients: hidden valley original ranch dips mix
steps: in a large mixing bowl , stir to combine: 2 cups flour , yeast , sugar , salt and dip mix
add evoo and water
stir with a wooden spoon until mixture comes together
knead in remaining flour
put dough into a clean oiled bowl and cover
let rest 20 minutes in a warm spot
while dough is resting: in a small mixing bowl
mix together ranch dressing and lemon zest
set aside
put prawns into a large zip-lock bag
add 1 teaspoons evoo and toss with prawns
mix together parmesan cheese and 1 teaspoons dip mix and add to bag of prawns
tossing to coat prawns well
set aside
when dough has rested 20minutes: preheat oven to 400
punch dough down and shape into a 13 inch circle on a pizza stone
cover and let rest 10 minutes
pre-cook pizza dough for 8-10 minutes
remove from oven and spread with lemon zesty ranch dressing
top with parmesan coated prawns
spacing them evenly on top of pizza
sprinkle with shredded cheese
mix together 1 tablespoons evoo and 1 teaspoons lemon juice and drizzle over the shredded cheese
bake at 400 for 7-9 minutes
when pizza comes out of the oven
sprinkle with chives
mangia !

reviews.comment: Oh yum! I'll have to try this pizza!!!!
Laurie , very good recipe !
Fantastic recipe Laurie!! Homemade pizza in just 48 minutes YUMMO : )
Great recipe!
Excellent!
Outstanding :)
Unique pizza and delicious!
AHHHHH, pizza comfort food!!!
So light and delicious!!!!! Perfect for a luncheon with salad...
Outta of this world DELICIOUS! sw
OOOhhh I bet this is good! I want to try asap!!! :o)
Very tasty!

name: garlic lemon chicken with green beans red potatoes
steps: directions
preheat oven to 400f coat a large baking dish or cast-iron skillet with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil
arrange the lemon slices in a single layer in the bottom of the dish or skillet
in a large bowl , combine the remaining oil , lemon juice , garlic , salt , and pepper
add the green beans and toss to coat
using a slotted spoon or tongs , remove the green beans and arrange them on top of the lemon slices
add the potatoes to the same olive-oil mixture and toss to coat
using a slotted spoon or tongs , arrange the potatoes along the inside edge of the dish or skillet on top of the green beans
place the chicken in the same bowl with the olive-oil mixture and coat thoroughly
place the chicken , skin-side up , in the dish or skillet
pour any of the remaining olive-oil mixture over the chicken
roast for 50 minutes
remove the chicken from the dish or skillet
place the beans and potatoes back in oven for 10 minutes more or until the potatoes are tender
place a chicken breast on each of 4 serving plates
divide the green beans and potatoes equally
serve warm

reviews.comment: Sounds delicious...unfortunately this was absolutely the most horrible chicken dish ever. Took a lot longer than 50 minutes for the chicken. The lemon only flavored the green beans which overpowered the flavor of the bean. The chicken had no flavor at all. The potatoes were just a weird texture and just blah. I have no suggestions to make this dish better because I think it's a lost cause. What a waste. It didn't even smell good while baking in the oven...I should have known then this was going to be a fail.

I have to admit.. it looks and sound so delish.. but, it was not. I was very disappointed with this dish. With all the negative feedback (on FB) that I read.. I tried to save it even before i baked it but it still was not great. On a scale of 1-10, I would give it a 3 I suppose. I am not going to give up though.. I will figure out a way to make it my own and make changes so it will be tasty and fabulous!!!!! (crossing my fingers)

Tweaking this recipe is simple.. marinate the chicken for a day then follow the rest of the instructions and it's great. If you don't marinate it but want it to have flavor add some of the sauce on the side or over the chicken after cooking. It is a wonderful recipe you to know how to work with it.

I have made this recipe several times and it is been a winner with everyone every time! Very simple easy to make and so tasteful. The only thing I do different is I cover it with foii for the first 50 minutes, then bake it for additional 20 minutes with the foil removed or loosely placed on top but not sealed. I have also made it an alternate way, without the bottom layers of lemons using only the juice of the first lemon. I do believe the placement of the chicken to the bottom of the baking dish is key in order to absorb the lemon juice for flavor and tenderizing.
Added parsley as a finishing touch, it was family hit. I'll have to double the recipe next time for 4 men and I.

I am giving this 5 stars because it looks and smells delicious--I am making it for a neighbor so haven't tasted. However, I used a 2-lb. package of chicken tenderloins, added a splash of white wine according to another reviewer, and added dried tarragon. I also covered it with foil for about 1/2 the cooking time, stirred it around a bit, and took the foil off. I added about 10-15 min. extra cooking time, too, just to make sure the potatoes were thoroughly cooked. Let's hope it's a hit!

My family loves this recipe. We have had this dish several times. The only change I make is placing the sliced lemons on top of the chicken. The beans tasted bitter when they directly touched the lemon. It's really easy and only one dish.

This dish was so quick and easy, I wanted it to be wonderful. The green beans were awful and the chicken was as bland as can be. Also, I found the lemon to be overpowering for the potatoes and green beans.
Delicious! It was done in under 50 minutes. Marinated early in the day and a wonderful lemon flavor and a definite keeper.

Make sure you marinate the chicken overnight! I added butter to my green beans and didn't add lemon juice to the potatoes. Place three slices on the bottom of the chicken and then placed the rest of the slices on the top part and it was amazing! Very flavorful love it

I started to make this in the oven but was starving & didn't want to wait for an hour to eat so pulled it out after 20 min & fried everything on the stove. I seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper, thyme, & basil before frying it to give it more flavor. It turned out delicious! I'm not sure how it would've turned out if I had left it in the oven but I could see the lemon over powering the green beans. However, I like my veggies close to burnt when I fry them & the green beans fried to almost brown paired nicely with the lemon. Will definitely make again!

I added fresh dill to the entire deal, and 3 extra cloves of garlic. I used chicken breasts instead, aswell as baby red potatoes cut into 3s, in a glass casserole dish uncovered and it turned out delicious. I coated everything in the lemon/garlic/dill mix and added dry dill on top of the chicken breast before putting in in the oven. The times were exact and it was a very effortless and refreshing (the lemon) dish. I also used plain Greek yogurt to dip the potatoes in, and because of the ingredients in the mixture, it felt like I was eating tzatziki. Has a very Greek feel.

I have done this recipe now over 20 times and people love it, I have tweaked it to perfection , chicken thighs bone in and marinate the day before in a bag and move around for a good soaking, important to have small waxy potatoes, I use thyme fresh or dry, good olive oil, don't bother about the green beans, cook them separately. I put potatoes one the bottom after layering a shallow lasagna type dish, chicken sits on the top, I cover and cook for 30mins then take foil off for last 20 mins, take chicken off and rest if potatoes are not quite cookeded, you can always add some more olive oil and this stage, chicken back in, bread for mopping up juices. I've added black olives sometimes, capers, when here in France for the summer the French love it!

We've made this three times now and it rocks. Things I've learned/ refined along the way, if it helps: 1) Slice the lemons THIN. You can eat them, peel and all, after they're cooked. If you don't like lemons, skip this. 2) SMALL red potatoes, quartered. You want them to caramelize and crisp in the hot oven, not bake into mushy bleh. 3) The lemon-oil mixture needs to coat everything—first the beans, then the potatoes, and then the chicken. Rub the chicken breasts in the remaining mixture so it's coated well on all sides. I didn't marinate the chicken ahead of time but made sure I did rub the chicken in the mixture, and it was perfecto. 4) Cook for 45 minutes (not 50), remove chicken, cook for 5-10 more. 5) Cook it all in one pan. The point of this recipe, IMO, is its ease. Separating everything out would add more pans and complexity. And for god's sake, use fresh green beans, not canned! Have fun, and enjoy!
